newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Venezuela oil strike ends without incident-PDVSA.
newsitem.headline: Venezuela oil strike ends without incident-PDVSA.

text.p: Venezuela's oil workers went back to work as scheduled at 1500 local time (1900 GMT) on Friday after an eight-hour strike which caused no disruption to supply or exports, a PDVSA spokesman said on Friday.

"Fortunately the stoppage was conducted peacefully and operations were maintained without any problems. We activated our contingency plans to operate the installations where workers were absent," said PDVSA human resources director Fernando Sanchez.
"We maintained our domestic supply service and there was no interruption in shipping."
He said the PDVSA operating subsidiaries, Corpoven, Maraven and Lagoven, planned to have negotiations with the unions over the weekend to avoid any further action.
A spokesman for Maraven's Cardon refinery said earlier that 89 percent of workers had turned up for work on Friday morning.
Fedepetrol union president Carlos Ortega said he planned to present a formal complaint to the employment ministry on Monday which could lead to an indefinite strike.

PDVSA's Sanchez said: "Tomorrow we will start negotiations with the unions to try to reach an agreement on the points which they have submitted. If we don't reach an accord, they have indicated they will present a strike plan to the employment ministry on Monday, but we hope it does not get to that."
Ortega says workers have 14 points of contention, including performance-related bonuses, inflation-related pay rises and contract worker wages.
